text: The 2021 loss of 81.3 hectares (2.23% of the asset) is corroborated by multiple independent sources. The University of Maryland's Global Forest Change dataset (GFC-2025-v1.13) observed this tree-cover loss in 2021. Additionally, the European Commission Joint Research Centre's Global Forest Cover 2020 (GFC2020) dataset confirms that 98% of the event area was mapped as forest in 2020, meeting the corroboration rule. The Uruguay Ministry of Livestock, Agriculture and Fisheries' National forest cartography (2021) further supports this by indicating that the loss occurred in planted forest areas, specifically Pinus elliottii and Pinus taeda. These sources collectively validate the observed loss.
